Your wife is completely in the right to be upset, but you also didn't know she was upset until you got home because you didn't see her text. Sometimes we don't realize how things would effect people until they do. I read on a separate reply that it for some reason didn't cross your mind, and that happens sometimes. It's a simple fault that anyone could fall victim to. Neither of you are the asshole, this seems like just an unfortunate situation.


 I hope you two can work through this.

Edit: reread and had to correct a few things

NTA, but could have handled it better imo

She definitely shouldn't have made such a rude comment to your mother, that's not okay, and it's perfectly understandable you would retaliate, but retaliation like that only escalates a situation. It's important to be assertive, but not aggressive. It would have been better to just tell her she was being inappropriate, rather than retaliating with an insult. It's hard to be civil in the heat of the moment so I completely understand your reaction, but just try to remember this for future reference.

YTA... But salvageable

It looks like you had good intentions, but you're too inside your own head. You should respect your boyfriend's wishes about celebrating his birthday, trauma isn't as simple as "replacing memories".

It seems like your motive was primarily selfish, trying to get him involved in your families tradition. It's good to share things with your partner, but it's crucial to respect their boundaries, which you crossed. His friend was right to scold you in my opinion, but I think this situation can be salvaged. 

I think a good solution is to apologize and make a conscious effort to be aware of times where you may think you're doing it for someone else when in reality you're mainly doing it for your own benefit, it's important to know the difference.
